findings.checklist_item: Qualify or drop the 'materialize only the paths the gate actually reads' option in AC1: the tickets tree is the agent's whole ticket-tools read root and the read set is not statically knowable, so a partial copy risks a silently-truncated attested store — state the completeness constraint each remaining option must satisfy.
evidence: gate_source.py:114 `with use_code_root(...), use_tickets_root(handle.tickets_path)` activates the whole tickets tree as the ticket-tools read root
SnapshotHandle docstring (repo_snapshot.py:187-190): tickets_path is 'the read root for the agent's rebar TICKET tools'
gate_resolve docstring (:85): 'an attested gate never silently reads the wrong tree' — a partial materialization can silently omit paths a later tool read needs
The gate resolves tickets ONCE up front (materialize_tickets at :99); the set of ticket ids/deps the agent will later query is unknown at materialize time
findings.finding: AC1 offers 'materialize only the paths the gate actually reads' as an equal alternative, but the tickets tree is activated as the agent's whole ticket-store read root (use_tickets_root at gate_source.py:114) and the rebar ticket tools read arbitrary tickets/deps/aliases at runtime — the read set is not statically knowable, so a partial materialization risks a truncated store and violates the fail-closed 'never silently reads the wrong tree' guarantee.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, AC1 (option 'materialize only the paths the gate actually reads')
scenarios: Implementer picks the partial-materialization option; agent queries a dependency ticket whose file was not pre-materialized and gets a missing/mis-resolved ticket instead of a fail-closed error

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency contract for the new reuse mechanism: how a review that hardlinks/reflinks against a prior entry avoids reading a neighbour that is still mid-materialize (atomic temp-dir+rename publish, or link only against a fully-committed entry), given the plan's own measured concurrent writers.
evidence: AC: 'hardlink/reflink against the prior entry, materialize only the paths the gate actually reads, or pin a coarser/stabler key'

Plan measures concurrent writers: 'The review-bot's own code_review artifact write ... guarantees the ref advances between reviews' and '1,374 commits in a 10-hour window ... the tip moves every ~26 seconds'
ABSENCE: no CREATE/UPDATE ownership or atomic-publish rule for the new reuse path is stated; a hardlink against a partially-materialized neighbour would consume a torn tree
findings.finding: The plan introduces a reuse mechanism (hardlink/reflink against the prior entry, or materialize-subset) over a cache store that is written by concurrent reviews across the fleet (the plan itself measures the tip moving every ~26s / 1,374 commits in 10h), but does not specify concurrency safety for the new mechanism: whether two reviews materializing adjacent tickets SHAs at the same time could hardlink/reflink against a neighbour entry that is still mid-write, or how atomic publish (temp-dir + rename) is preserved.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, bullet 1 (hardlink/reflink against the prior entry / materialize only the paths the gate reads)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] For whichever link/subset approach is chosen, specify the fallback and error surfacing when the link operation is unsupported (reflink on ext4/Windows) or cross-device (store vs REBAR_TRACKER_DIR on different mounts), so failures degrade safely and are observable rather than silently regressing to full copies.
evidence: AC offers 'hardlink/reflink against the prior entry' as a repair option
Plan cites 'tracker_dir_override() ... returns REBAR_TRACKER_DIR verbatim' — the tracker dir can be on a different mount than the snapshot store, across which hardlinks fail (EXDEV)
ABSENCE: no error-handling / fallback for link-unsupported or partial-link states
findings.finding: The plan adds new filesystem write operations (hardlink or reflink into the content-addressed store) without addressing their failure modes: reflink is unsupported on many filesystems (ext4, common Windows filesystems) and hardlinks fail across mount boundaries when the store and REBAR_TRACKER_DIR live on different devices. The plan names these as options but specifies no fallback/degraded-mode or error surfacing when the link operation is unavailable or fails partway.

findings.checklist_item: Add per-option correctness caveats to AC1 — require a defined full-copy fallback if reflink/FICLONE is unavailable on the deployment fs, and require that any 'coarser/stabler key' preserves ADR 0005's per-SHA read-correctness (no two distinct ticket trees sharing one entry).
evidence: _materialize_tree writes a fresh tree via git checkout-index (repo_snapshot.py:373-410) with no delta/link mechanism today, so hardlink/reflink is net-new infrastructure whose fs support is unverified

AC1 asks the approach be 'justified against ADR 0005's integrity guarantees' but a coarser key by construction breaks the 'immutable SHA is a perfect cache key' basis the Why-this-is-a-defect section cites
Plan states no fallback behavior when reflink is unavailable
findings.finding: The two remaining AC1 options carry unstated correctness caveats the plan should surface so the implementer's rationale can address them: reflink/hardlink is filesystem-capability-dependent (FICLONE may be unsupported on the review-bot's fs) and needs a defined fallback, and 'pin a coarser/stabler key' directly weakens ADR 0005's SHA-immutability integrity property.
scenarios: Reflink chosen; review-bot root fs lacks FICLONE support, silently falling back to full copies and not fixing the bug
Coarser key chosen; two tickets SHAs collide onto one entry and an attested gate reads a stale/wrong ticket tree

findings.checklist_item: Name the sibling ticket and record an explicit dependency edge (or cite it `<subject> [rebar:<C>]`), and state the accounting API AC#3 must call, so the criterion is verifiable within this ticket.
evidence: 'materialize_tickets participates in the store's byte accounting (see the sibling ticket)'
no ticket id / [rebar:<C>] citation for the sibling ticket
fail-closed: an uncited cross-ticket reference is graded as item-9
findings.finding: AC#3 makes completion depend on byte-accounting machinery attributed to 'the sibling ticket' but names no ticket id and declares no dependency edge, so the criterion is not self-contained or verifiable within this ticket.
scenarios: The byte-accounting hook does not yet exist when this ticket is implemented, so AC#3 cannot be satisfied or measured in-session
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'see the sibling ticket' with the concrete ticket id and add a depends_on edge, then state the byte-accounting entry point (e.g. the store method that records entry bytes) that materialize_tickets must invoke.

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile AC#2's '~1 tree' metric with each AC#1 approach — state the expected footprint per approach (e.g. bytes-below-threshold rather than tree-count) so the test matches whichever path is chosen.
evidence: AC#1 option 2: 'materialize only the paths the gate actually reads'
AC#2: 'N reviews across N adjacent tickets SHAs consume ~1 tree, not N trees'
the two ACs assume different disk-usage shapes
findings.finding: AC#2's success metric ('N reviews consume ~1 tree, not N trees') presupposes the reuse/hardlink approach; if the executor chooses AC#1's 'materialize only the paths the gate reads' option, each review still writes a distinct partial materialization and the '~1 tree' assertion no longer describes the fix.
scenarios: Executor narrows materialization, satisfies the intent, but AC#2's specific '~1 tree' assertion fails to match the resulting footprint

findings.checklist_item: State a preferred approach (or ranked default) among the three AC#1 options, so the executor need not adjudicate a real design fork mid-implementation.
evidence: 'hardlink/reflink against the prior entry, materialize only the paths the gate actually reads, or pin a coarser/stabler key'
each option has materially different testing and doc implications
the 'justified against ADR 0005' clause bounds but does not resolve the choice
findings.finding: AC#1 defers a real architectural choice among three structurally different approaches (hardlink/reflink against prior entry, narrow materialization to gate-read paths, or re-key to a coarser/stabler key) without ranking or a stated default, leaving the executor to pick.
scenarios: Executor picks narrow-materialization while author intended hardlinking, invalidating AC#2's 'consume ~1 tree' framing
findings.suggested_fix: Rank the options (e.g. 'prefer hardlink/reflink against the prior entry as the default; fall back to coarser-key only if reflink is unavailable on the store filesystem') so the choice is a stated default the executor can act on.

findings.checklist_item: Confirm what byte-accounting work AC-3 actually requires given materialize_tickets already calls add_bytes(entry_size(dest)) at repo_snapshot.py:702-715, so the fix extends rather than rebuilds it.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:702-715: 'from rebar._snapshot.cache import add_bytes as _add_bytes ... _add_bytes(_entry_size(dest), store)' on the populate (race-won) branch

Inline comment at :702-706: 'The ticket-store entries are the largest thing in the store, and without this the janitor's running byte total ... simply cannot see them. Mirrors cache.acquire's add_bytes on its own populate branch'
Plan AC-3 defers to 'the sibling ticket' without stating what accounting gap remains given the existing add_bytes call
findings.finding: AC-3 asks to make materialize_tickets 'participate in the store's byte accounting ... so the entries it creates are visible to any size-based reclaim', deferring to 'the sibling ticket' — but the populate branch of materialize_tickets already calls add_bytes(entry_size(dest), store) at repo_snapshot.py:702-715 (with the cache-hit and lost-race branches deliberately not accounting). If that accounting is already live, AC-3 risks re-specifying / rebuilding existing functionality (NIH) or double-counting across two tickets; the plan should confirm what is actually missing versus already present.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, bullet 3 ('materialize_tickets participates in the store's byte accounting')
scenarios: Author implements AC-3 as a fresh add_bytes wiring, duplicating the existing :702-715 call and double-counting bytes
Sibling ticket and this ticket both claim ownership of the same already-implemented accounting

findings.checklist_item: Reconcile AC-3 with repo_snapshot.py:713, which already calls `add_bytes(entry_size(dest), store)` in `materialize_tickets`: state whether byte accounting is genuinely missing on the target branch or whether AC-3 should instead cover only the reduced/hardlinked entry sizes that the AC-1 repair introduces.
evidence: repo_snapshot.py:709-715: `from rebar._snapshot.cache import add_bytes as _add_bytes` / `_add_bytes(_entry_size(dest), store)` on the populate branch
In-code comment (702-706): 'We WON the populate race, so account this entry's bytes exactly once... Mirrors cache.acquire's add_bytes'
AC-3 phrasing '(see the sibling ticket) so the entries it creates are visible to any size-based reclaim' presupposes the accounting is absent
findings.finding: AC-3 requires that `materialize_tickets` be made to 'participate in the store's byte accounting', implying it does not today — but the current `materialize_tickets` already calls `add_bytes(entry_size(dest), store)` on its populate branch (repo_snapshot.py:713), with an in-code comment attributing that accounting to a sibling ticket. On the tree under review this AC's premise is refuted; the work may already be done (or the plan is written against an older snapshot).
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, bullet 3 ('materialize_tickets participates in the store's byte accounting')
scenarios: Implementer reads AC-3, discovers the add_bytes call already exists, and is unsure whether to no-op the criterion or whether the plan targets a pre-sibling snapshot
